plan.opening_note: My notes say hand-shaping the Montgomery arithmetic loses to LLVM, and that the msm inner-loop doubling fold only reached 0.9940 on its own. So this time I'll look at msm setup and other per-call costs, and pair any small saving with a second one on the same path rather than repeat those tries.

hypotheses: My notes say hand-shaping the Montgomery arithmetic loses to LLVM, and that the msm inner-loop doubling fold only reached 0.9940 on its own. So this time I'll look at msm setup and other per-call costs, and pair any small saving with a second one on the same path rather than repeat those tries.
`naf_entry` takes a fixed-size array, but `chunks_exact` yields slices, so I'll inline the lookup instead.
The `Sub` change makes no difference; the fold alone gives 0.9938. To close the remaining gap I need to see how big the msm bench inputs are.
The msm bench also runs double-scalar multiplications (ECDSA-style u1·G + u2·Q). The generator table might allow a wider window, so I'll check how it is built.
No room there: a width-9 NAF needs digits above ±127, which don't fit in `i8`. Field multiply and square dominate every path, so I'll check whether squaring also uses the cheaper shifted reduction.
I'll revert the `Sub` change, since it measured neutral, to keep the diff small. Then evaluate.

actions.reason:
I found no change that clears the 1% minimum on msm_ir. Three sandbox evaluations, all with identical outputs:

journal.text:
Target was msm_ir in secp256r1. First try: in group.rs I folded the per-iteration doubling in multi_scalar_mul_vartime into the first nonzero digit via double_add_mixed, and rewrote double() to get Z3 as (Y+Z)^2 - Y^2 - Z^2. Later tries touched field.rs squaring paths around montgomery_square.

Evaluation 1 gave msm_ir ratio 1.0152 and scalar_mul_ir 1.0416. Rejected. Evaluation 3, with group.rs and field.rs edits over 28 lines, reached msm_ir 0.9938. That is better than parent but short of the required 0.9900. Evaluation 5 regressed to msm_ir 1.0108 and scalar_mul_ir 1.0185. All three had identical outputs. No candidate was submitted.

In this field code a squaring costs about the same as a multiply. Swapping a multiply for squarings does not pay and can cost. The gains left in the msm loop structure look smaller than 1%.

Next, look at the cost of the wnaf table build and add_naf_digit per call rather than at doubling formulas. Also check whether the generator table can be reused across calls.
